R0185.title: Virtual World Asset Theft
R0185.definition: Illegal theft or transfer of users' virtual assets (equipment, items, currency, NFTs, etc.) in the metaverse.
R0185.description: Virtual assets in the metaverse have real economic value, making them targets for attackers. Theft methods include: exploiting smart contract vulnerabilities to transfer NFT assets, obtaining wallet private keys through social engineering, hacking game servers to steal items, exploiting trading system vulnerabilities to duplicate assets, phishing websites to induce authorization, etc. The digital nature of virtual assets makes them easy to steal in bulk and quickly transfer, with cross-border tracking being difficult.
R0185.influence: User virtual property losses, metaverse economic system imbalance, platform reputation damage.

observables: User NFTs or virtual assets are transferred to unfamiliar addresses without authorized operations
Game servers or trading systems show signs of asset duplication exploitation, with assets created out of thin air
Phishing websites induce users to sign authorizations for malicious contracts, after which virtual assets are bulk-transferred out
Stolen virtual assets are rapidly split and transferred across multiple addresses, ultimately entering mixers or over-the-counter trading
